label: accepted

evidence.V1: Plank top on four turned legs with an H-stretcher reads as a table from front, three-quarter, top (four boards with bolt heads) and silhouette; outline symmetric, A15 error 0.0 on X and Y.
evidence.V2: Clear: big = plank top and leg frame, medium = turned leg profiles, apron and H-stretcher, small = ink bolt heads, board chamfers and leg foot rings.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised proportions: chunky overhanging boards, bulbous turned legs with pinched waists and flared feet; slightly low and long (7.3 x 3.1 studs) so it borders on bench-like, but still reads as a table.
evidence.V4: Consistent chamfers on every board edge and the top rim that catch the light (apron_corner, top_boards close-ups); legs are smoothly turned.
evidence.V5: Clean: smooth gradients on boards and legs in studio and flat light, no pinches, seams or z-fighting; only mild polygonal outline on leg bulbs.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: wood hue in 3 values (light/mid boards, dark apron/stretcher) plus ink bolt heads; painted colourways keep the value structure.
evidence.V7: 1796 tris vs medium target 2000 / ceiling 4000 - under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, weighted smooth shading, ~0.05-stud chamfers, wood hue with ink iron accents - matches the furniture kit spec.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Box, CanTouch off, CastShadow on, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

top_fixes: Raise the top slightly or shorten the length so it reads less like a bench next to the chair
Add a few more radial segments to the leg bulbs/feet to soften their polygonal outline at close range
Optionally add a gold or ink fitting (corner bracket) to tie in the kit accent colour
